newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-N Brown new favourite to win Freemans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-N Brown new favourite to win Freemans.

text.p: British home shopping firm N. Brown Group Plc became the frontrunner to buy Freemans mail order business from Sears Plc after Sears confirmed on Thursday the two were in talks on a sale.
N. Brown emerged as a favourite to buy Britain's third biggest mail order company last week after Littlewoods LWD.CN LWD.CN pulled out of the negotiations.
The company asked for its shares to be suspended on Thursday afternoon until the two sides reached agreement on the sale.

N. Brown's shares have been under pressure because of the rights issue fears and were suspended at 377.5 pence, down four pence. Sears shares ended the day unchanged at 80 pence after trading within a very narrow range between 79 pence and 82.5 pence.
Littlewoods had agreed to buy Freemans in January for 395 million pounds ($630.8 million), but the acquisition was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission on competition grounds.

Littlewoods then withdrew when it emerged Sears was talking to other possible buyers. Sears said it could not give exclusivity to Littlewoods after it had received other offers and wanted to consider the best in the interests of shareholders.
Manchester-based N.Brown said Freemans would expand its market, giving it access to a younger customer base, which would complement its own direct mail catalogues aimed at older customers.

Analysts said if the deal went ahead N.Brown was expected to fund part of it with a rights issue, possibly up to about 250 million pounds. N.Brown had no comment on speculation about the rights issue.
Industry sources said this deal was less at risk from a monopoly investigation as N.Brown has just four percent of the British home shopping market.
They said if the sale went through this would help Sears try to fulfil plans to hand back cash to shareholders by the summer, analysts said.
"They could still do the cash return by the summer," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.
Sears has promised a 410 million pound payout to placate shareholders who have been dissatisfied with its performance.
The retailer, which also owns Selfridges department store in London, issued a profits warning in January after a disappointing Christmas.
Last year, plans to sell off its loss-making shoe business foundered when the buyer, privately-owned Facia, collapsed.
Analysts said Freemans would make N.Brown the number three in home shopping in Britain after Great Universal Stores Plc and Littlewoods.
